CORAM: THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE RAVI V.HOSMANI  ORAL JUDGMENT
With consent of learned counsel for parties, matter is taken up for disposal.

2. Challenging judgment and award dated 22.11.2017 passed in MVC no.2327/2015 by Senior Civil Judge and Addl. MACT, Bailhongal (for short, 'Tribunal'), this appeal is filed.
3.
Smt.Priyanka K., advocate appearing for Sri Madanmohan M.Khannur, learned counsel for appellant submitted that appeal was by claimant for enhancement of compensation.

It was submitted, in an accident that occurred on 19.08.2014, claimant travelling in Cruiser vehicle bearing no.KA-23/M-6033 from Marakumbi to Lingadalli Village along with others sustained grievous injuries when it collided with another Maxi Cab no.KA-26/2903.

Despite taking treatment at NC:
2026:KHC-D:3379 HC-KAR Malaprabha Multi Specialty Hospital, Bailhongal, he sustained loss of Shri.Yallappa S/O Gatigeppa Totagi vs Shri. Nijalingappa Gangappa Betageri on 4 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119010088/
2 earning capacity.

sentences.text: Therefore, he filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against owner and insurer of vehicles.
4. Said claim petition was clubbed with other claim petitions arising out of same accident.
On appearance, claim petition was opposed on all counts.
5. Based on pleadings, Tribunal framed issues and recorded evidence.
Claimant deposed as PW5 along with Dr.M.S.Mudakanagoudar as PW10 and got marked Exhibits P1 to P110.

Respondent - insurer examined its official as RW1 and got marked Exhibits R1 to R4.
6.

On consideration, Tribunal held accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of a Cruiser vehicle and claimant was entitled for compensation of 1,43,482/- with 9% interest from respondent - insurer.
Claim petition was dismissed against others.

Dissatisfied with quantum,
claimant was in appeal.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3379 HC-KAR 7.

It was submitted, claimant was 52 year old agriculturalist earning 2,00,000/- per year who sustained fracture of left elbow and right knee rightly assessed by PW10 to have resulted in 20% +
20% permanent physical disability in disability certificate.
Despite same, Tribunal considered monthly income of claimant at 7,000/- and assessed only 12% physical disability and awarded meagre compensation.

It was submitted that compensation of 20,000/- towards pain and suffering was also on lower side and Tribunal failed to award any compensation towards loss of amenities,
loss of income during laid up period and future medical expenses.
On said ground sought enhancement.
8. On other hand, Sri M.K.Soudagar, learned counsel for respondent - insurer opposed appeal.
It was submitted, Tribunal had considered entire material on record and awarded just compensation leaving no scope for enhancement.

9. Heard learned counsel and perused impugned judgment and award.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3379 HC-KAR 10.

From above and since only claimant is in appeal for enhancement of compensation, point that would arise for consideration is:
'Whether claimant is entitled for enhancement of compensation as prayed for?'
11.

Though claimant stated that he was 52 years of age doing agriculture and earning 2,00,000/-
per year, same was not substantiated with specific evidence.
In absence, Tribunal would be justified in assessing it notionally.

However, notional income for year of accident i.e. 2014 being 7,500/-,
Tribunal was not justified in taking it at 7,000/-.

sentences.text: 3 12. In Ex.P91 - Disability Certificate, PW10 assessed disability on account of two fractural injuries to be at 20% + 20%.
However, there is no reference to assessment of loss of earning capacity.
There is also no reference to extent of restriction of movement caused by malunion of fractures.

On examination of entire material on record and Tribunal arrived at conclusion that assessment of permanent physical disability by PW10 was excessive and moderated it to have caused 12% loss of earning capacity.
In absence of demonstration that NC: 2026:KHC-D:3379 HC-KAR assessment was contrary to material on record, this Court is not inclined to vary disability.
Multiplier applicable for age 52 is '11'.

Thus, recalculation of compensation towards future loss of income would be :
7,500 x 12% x 12 x 11 = 1,18,800/-.
13.
Claimant sustained fracture of left elbow and right knee i.e. two grievous fractures.
Therefore, it is found appropriate to enhance compensation towards pain and suffering to 50,000/-.
Tribunal awarded 10,802/- towards medical expenses and 1,800/- towards incidental expenses in reimbursement of value of bills produced.
Same would not call for modification.
However, Tribunal has not awarded any compensation towards loss of amenities and loss of income during laid up period.
Normally, fractures take three months to heal.
Taking same as layoff period, compensation of 22,500/- is awarded towards loss of income during laid up period.
Taking note of fact that claimant sustained two fractural injuries and sustained disability on both, it is found appropriate to award 35,000/- towards loss of amenities.
There is no reference to insertions of implants and requirement of further surgery for NC: 2026:KHC-D:3379 HC-KAR removal.

In absence of same,
there would be no justification for claim for future medical expenses.

Thus, total reassessed compensation is :
 Loss of future income 1,18,800/-
 Pain and suffering 50,000/-

Medical expenses 10,802/-
 Incidental expenses 1,800/-
 Loss of income during laid up period 22,500/-
 Loss of amenities 35,000/-
 Total 2,38,902/-
14.
Consequently, point for consideration is answered partly in affirmative.

15. In view of above, following:
ORDER i. Appeal is allowed in part.
ii. Claimant is entitled enhanced compensation of Rs.2,38,902/- as against Rs.1,43,482/- awarded by Tribunal.
Same shall carry interest at 9% p.a. from date of petition till date of deposit.
